A bench for the story

A short Krownlandia story to read silently or aloud.

On the way to Town Square, Mina kept one hand over the paper boat in her pocket. It had a blue sail and a crease down the middle where she had changed her mind about which end was the front.

The square was full of voices. At the stage, someone was telling a story about the river. Mina could hear the beginning whenever the wind turned toward her. She missed the middle every time.

At the bench, a neighbor was drawing. Mina sat beside them and unfolded the boat. “What did I miss?” she asked.

The neighbor turned the page around. There were three pictures: a bridge, a boat, and a shore. “I missed some words too,” they said. “I drew what I heard. I’m still waiting to find out which way the boat went.”

Mina placed her paper boat between the bridge and the shore. “Perhaps it stopped to pick somebody up.”

When the storyteller finished, she came over to see the drawings. She left space on the page beside the shore. “That’s a good place to start tomorrow’s story,” she said.

Try telling the story another way

Retell it with three sounds, three short lines, or three pictures. Keep the same beginning and change what the neighbors find at the end. If you’re reading together, take turns choosing one detail to keep.

This is a new story for the prototype, inspired by the Krownlandia Book Store idea credited to @ThomasMDelonge in the historical inventory (page 15). The characters and events are fictional.
